title: Can't remap Windows + C and other 'hard-coded' shortcuts

status.label: Needs a current system-shortcut comparison
status.detail: The Win+C behavior overlaps an existing Copilot-key report, while the separate Teams shortcut has not been isolated from Windows handling.

next_action.label: Check both shortcuts with Keyboard Manager disabled
next_action.reason: A current enabled/disabled comparison will separate the Copilot-key report from the distinct Teams shortcut and determine which layer handles each chord.

actions.label: Check both shortcuts with Keyboard Manager disabled

comment.body: Thanks for giving the Windows 11 25H2 version and both outcomes. The Win+C-to-Settings behavior is already reported in #46301, which was closed as a duplicate of #35808; that does not cover the separate Win+Shift+Ctrl+Alt+T-to-Teams behavior. Could you confirm whether each shortcut still does this on v0.102.3001 when Keyboard Manager is disabled and when PowerToys is fully exited? Also, is the first input a physical Copilot key or a literal Win+C chord, and does the second shortcut still launch Teams in both tests?

judgment.rationale: The report is from v0.99.1 on Windows 11 25H2 and describes two outcomes: Win+C opens the Windows Copilot-key settings page, while Win+Shift+Ctrl+Alt+T launches Teams. The first behavior closely matches #46301, which was closed as a duplicate of the still-open #35808; it should not be treated as a new independent Copilot-key fix. The distinct Teams behavior is not covered by that thread, and the report does not say whether it occurs with Keyboard Manager disabled or PowerToys exited.
evidence: The issue lists PowerToys v0.99.1 and Windows 11 25H2.
The body says remapping Win+C to calc.exe opens Windows Settings at the Copilot-key customization page instead.
The alternative Win+Shift+Ctrl+Alt+T mapping reportedly opens Microsoft Teams.
Issue #46301 reports the same Win+C/Copilot settings behavior and was closed as a duplicate of #35808, which remains open.
No assignee or matching PR was found for #47950.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for a current comparison with Keyboard Manager disabled and PowerToys exited, and confirm whether the input is a physical Copilot key or the Win+C chord.

fix_assessment.rationale: The Copilot-key portion is tracked elsewhere, but the separate Teams shortcut may be another Windows- or application-owned chord. If current testing shows PowerToys intercepts it yet the original action still fires, the remapping path may need to suppress the original shortcut; the handling layer is not yet established.

proposed_fixes.title: Handle only confirmed PowerToys-owned system shortcut conflicts
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Windows may handle one or both chords before the requested Keyboard Manager action takes effect. The Win+C behavior is already tracked by #35808; the report provides no enabled/disabled comparison for the distinct Teams shortcut.
plan: Compare both chords on current stable with Keyboard Manager enabled, disabled, and PowerToys exited.
For any remaining PowerToys-owned mapping failure, trace whether the original OS/application shortcut is still delivered after the remapped action.
Use a supported Windows integration path only for confirmed OS-owned shortcuts; otherwise keep the existing remapping path and explain the limitation.
Add regression coverage for the confirmed Win+C and Teams-chord behavior without duplicating the Copilot-key work tracked in #35808.
verification: Confirm the current enabled/disabled behavior for both input chords and the exact action each opens.
Verify any PowerToys-owned remap suppresses the original action while unrelated Windows shortcuts remain unchanged.

confidence.rationale: The issue gives exact chords and outcomes, and the Copilot-key symptom has a direct related report, but the distinct Teams behavior and the layer that handles either chord are unverified.

issue_context.summary: Two Windows shortcuts reportedly bypass remapping: Win+C opens the Copilot-key settings page, and Win+Shift+Ctrl+Alt+T starts Teams.
known_information: The report lists PowerToys v0.99.1 on Windows 11 25H2.
Win+C is configured to launch calc.exe but instead opens Windows Settings at the Copilot-key customization page.
Win+Shift+Ctrl+Alt+T is reported to launch Teams instead of the selected target.
Issue #46301 reports the same Win+C/Copilot settings behavior and was closed as a duplicate of #35808; #35808 remains open.
The report does not include an enabled/disabled comparison, screenshot, or current-version retest.
inferences: The Win+C symptom may be the same Windows Copilot-key handling tracked in #35808 rather than an independent Keyboard Manager defect.
The Teams shortcut may be owned by Windows, Teams, or the input device, but the issue does not identify which layer handles it.
issue_context.analysis: The two shortcuts should not be collapsed into one defect. The Win+C behavior has an existing open tracking issue, while the Teams shortcut is a distinct, unverified case. A current comparison with Keyboard Manager disabled and PowerToys exited is the smallest test that determines whether a separate PowerToys fix is justified.
initial_investigation: Refreshed the complete issue body and comment, including the version, Windows 11 25H2, both input chords, and both actual outcomes.
Compared the Win+C symptom with #46301 and its duplicate target #35808; did not treat the duplicate closure as a fix.
Searched for reports or PRs for the exact Teams chord; none were found.
Confirmed the issue has no assignee.

information_gaps.information: Whether both shortcut outcomes persist on v0.102.3001 with Keyboard Manager disabled and with PowerToys fully exited, and whether Win+C comes from a physical Copilot key or a literal chord
information_gaps.why_needed: This determines whether Windows or another component owns the behavior and whether the distinct Teams shortcut needs separate PowerToys investigation.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: On v0.102.3001, test each chord with Keyboard Manager enabled, then disabled, then with PowerToys exited; report what opens and whether the first input is a physical Copilot key or Win+C.
